Appearance
From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • emphasise (Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, UK)

Etymology

[edit]

Latin, from Ancient Greek – see emphasis.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (UK) IPA(key): /ˈɛm.fə.saɪz/, [ˈɛɱ.fə.saɪz]
  • Audio (US):(file)

Verb

[edit]

emphasize (third-person singular simple present emphasizes, present participle emphasizing, simple past and past participle emphasized)

  1. (transitive) To stress, give emphasis or extra weight to (something).
    His two-fingered gesture emphasized what he had told his boss to do with his job.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • betone
  • highlight
  • stress
  • underscore

Antonyms

[edit]
  • de-emphasize
  • downplay

Derived terms

[edit]
  • deëmphasize
  • emphasizable
  • emphasization
  • emphasize everything and nothing is emphasized
  • emphasizer
  • hyperemphasize
  • misemphasize
  • overemphasize
  • reemphasize
  • to emphasize everything is to emphasize nothing
  • underemphasize

Related terms

[edit]
  • emphasis
  • emphatic
